parts.text:
Revise the CURRENT Agents.md and CURRENT send-to-gemini.js TOGETHER to correct all supervisory-gating and per-step return-schema control failures uncovered in the recent runs. Produce a paired revision, not an evaluation-only response and not a runtime-only revision. The revised specification and runtime must agree exactly.

The user's governing correction must be quoted verbatim in your revision analysis and used as the central design/control requirement:

"Use the eval branch to require gemini to revise Agents.md and sourcecode together to correct all gating issues. No no youve got that wrong, return schema refers to the specifc schema for that step. 
And thats the central fucking control 
Its the thing the model should communicate through 
no communciation should occur without the return schema for that step thats why threyre fucking listed every step"

Interpret that correction literally in the architecture: every procedure step has its own required return schema; that step's semantic operator communicates its result/completion only through that schema; no step may communicate successful completion, advancement, or substitute prose/object outside that required return schema. The supervisor must evaluate that exact step return schema before any later step may execute. If that schema is missing, malformed, incomplete, mismatched to the step/user request/run identity, or not persisted as required, the gate is FAIL and the SAME STEP must be repaired/re-run until it returns a valid schema and passes. No later output can cure an earlier failed gate.

Correct the meaning of return_schema_completed everywhere. It refers to completion of THE SPECIFIC RETURN SCHEMA FOR THAT STEP, not completion of the whole multi-step procedure. Therefore when a step has successfully produced its required return schema, return_schema_completed must be true. A false value means that step's schema is not complete and cannot pass its gate or advance. Revise Agents.md and runtime logic together to make this unambiguous and mechanically enforced.

Also incorporate all previously identified gating requirements: preserve the external user utterance verbatim and keep internal controller prompts separate; initialize the supervisory evaluation template neutrally with null evaluative/result fields before supervisor evaluation; require the supervisor to granularly evaluate every returned key/array entry plus the step as a whole; require exact transition keys without permissive fallback paths unless explicitly specified; missing/invalid required transition output must invoke repair rather than advancement; Step 3 must honor its evaluation-document requirements and loop semantics; FAIL must restart the same execution step; PASS alone may advance; the actual user-requested deliverable must be evaluated against every stated requirement; and a completed procedure with N defined steps must have at least N durable Git commits attributable to the run, with each completed step/gate boundary persisted and committed before advancing, otherwise completion is automatically FAIL.

The revised Agents.md must include concrete mechanical examples sufficient to prevent inference errors, including at least: a valid Step 0 execution return with return_schema_completed:true; an invalid/incomplete Step 0 return that must FAIL; an unevaluated supervisory input/template; a completed PASS supervisory return; a completed FAIL supervisory return with failures recorded; same-step repair/retry after FAIL; Step 3 loop behavior; and per-step durable commit/checkpoint behavior.

Return the complete non-truncated replacement Agents.md in revised_agents_md and the complete non-truncated replacement send-to-gemini.js in revised_program. Do not provide patches or ellipses. Do not leave known gating discrepancies unresolved.
